title: Tor independence for an algebraic-space product square with two flat sides
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$, their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], and the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $Z_0\to X_0$, $Z_0\to Y_0$, $X_0\to B_0$, and $Y_0\to B_0$ be a commutative square of algebraic spaces. Let $B\to B_0$ be any morphism of algebraic spaces and put $X=X_0\times_{B_0}B$, $Y=Y_0\times_{B_0}B$, $P_0=X_0\times_{B_0}Y_0$ and $P=X\times_BY$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Assume $Y_0\to B_0$ and $Z_0\to X_0$ are flat, meaning flat on compatible etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Then $Z_0\to P_0$ and $P\to P_0$ are Tor independent: for every commutative diagram of geometric points $\bar z:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Z_0$ and $\bar p:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P$ with the same composite $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P_0$, where $\Omega$ is algebraically closed,
$$\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal O_{P_0,\bar t}}_n(\mathcal O_{Z_0,\bar z},\mathcal O_{P,\bar p})=0\qquad(n>0).$$
Geometric local rings are stalks on the small etale site; Tor is computed by projective resolutions [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. No cartesianness of the original square, closed immersion, flatness of $B\to B_0$ or $X_0\to B_0$, or finiteness assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 0CTQ, lemma-case-of-tor-independence; geometric-stalk meaning spelled out as in spaces-perfect.tex, definition-tor-independent.

proof.text: Choose surjective etale scheme atlases $W_0\to B_0$, $W\to B\times_{B_0}W_0$, $U_0\to X_0\times_{B_0}W_0$ and $V_0\to Y_0\times_{B_0}W_0$. Put $Q_0=U_0\times_{W_0}V_0$, and choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $T_0\to Z_0\times_{P_0}Q_0$. Atlas existence is part of the definition of algebraic space. The map $Q_0\to P_0\times_{B_0}W_0$ factors as the base change of the $U_0$ atlas and then the base change of the $V_0$ atlas. Thus $Q_0\to P_0$ is surjective etale by base change and composition of etale coverings. Likewise $U_0\to X_0$ and $V_0\to Y_0$ are surjective etale. The fibre-product equations identify $Z_0\times_{P_0}Q_0$ with $(Z_0\times_{X_0}U_0)\times_{Y_0\times_{B_0}W_0}V_0$. Consequently $T_0\to Z_0\times_{X_0}U_0$ is surjective etale. All these fibre products are schemes whenever both factors over an algebraic space are schemes, by representability of its diagonal.

source.place: Tag 0CTQ, lemma-case-of-tor-independence, proof and detailed etale-chart footnote.

proof.text: Apply the flat chart test to $Y_0\to B_0$, using the target chart $W_0$ and source chart $V_0$: it gives flatness of $V_0\to W_0$. Apply it to $Z_0\to X_0$, using the target chart $U_0\to X_0$ and source chart $T_0\to Z_0\times_{X_0}U_0$ constructed in step 1: it gives flatness of $T_0\to U_0$. The projection $Q_0\to U_0$ is the scheme base change of $V_0\to W_0$, so it is flat. Thus $T_0$ and $Q_0$ are two flat schemes over the common base $U_0$, and the induced map $T_0\to Q_0$ is a $U_0$-morphism. No flatness of this last map is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0CTQ, lemma-case-of-tor-independence, proof and detailed etale-chart footnote.

proof.text: Set $A=U_0\times_{W_0}W$ and $Q=Q_0\times_{W_0}W$. Apply the existing flat-family Tor-independence theorem over the scheme $U_0$, with its $X=T_0$, $Y=Q_0$, morphism $T_0\to Q_0$ and arbitrary base change $S'=A\to U_0$. Step 2 verifies exactly its two flatness hypotheses. The fibre-product universal property identifies $Q_0\times_{U_0}A$ with $Q$: a section on either side is a triple $(u_0,v_0,w)$ with equal images in $W_0$. Hence for every ordinary $t\in T_0$ and $q\in Q$ over the same $q_0\in Q_0$, the cited theorem gives $\operatorname{Tor}^{\mathcal O_{Q_0,q_0}}_i(\mathcal O_{T_0,t},\mathcal O_{Q,q})=0$ for all $i>0$.

source.place: Tag 0CTA, lemma-case-of-tor-independence: cartesian square over X-prime; use the existing common-flat-base scheme lemma.

proof.text: The universal property identifies $P=X\times_BY$ with $P_0\times_{B_0}B$: both have sections $(x_0,y_0,b)$ whose images in $B_0$ agree. It also identifies $Q$ with $(P\times_{P_0}Q_0)\times_{B\times_{B_0}W_0}W$, preserving the projections to $Q_0$. Therefore $Q\to P\times_{P_0}Q_0$ is a surjective etale scheme atlas, being the base change of $W\to B\times_{B_0}W_0$. Use the geometric Tor-independence chart criterion with $H=P_0$, $F=Z_0$, $G=P$, and atlases $W=Q_0$, $U=T_0$, $V=Q$. Their covering hypotheses were verified in steps 1 and 4. Step 3 is precisely its ordinary local-ring Tor condition. Its other equivalent condition is the asserted vanishing for every pair of geometric points of $Z_0$ and $P$ over $P_0$.

lean.statement: theorem product_torIndependent {S : Scheme.{u}} {Z₀ X₀ Y₀ B₀ B P₀ P : AlgebraicSpace S} (zX : Z₀ ⟶ X₀) (zY : Z₀ ⟶ Y₀) (f : X₀ ⟶ B₀) (g : Y₀ ⟶ B₀) (comm : zX ≫ f = zY ≫ g) (a : B ⟶ B₀) (r : P₀ ⟶ X₀) (s : P₀ ⟶ Y₀) (hP₀ : IsPullback r.hom s.hom f.hom g.hom) (p : P ⟶ P₀) (b : P ⟶ B) (hP : IsPullback p.hom b.hom (r ≫ f).hom a.hom) (hg : MapIsFlat g) (hzX : MapIsFlat zX) : IsGeometricallyTorIndependent (ObjectProperty.homMk (hP₀.lift zX.hom zY.hom (congrArg InducedCategory.Hom.hom comm))) p
lean.note: Uses the canonical projection-preserving identification X ×_B Y ≅ P₀ ×_{B₀} B. IsPullback witnesses specify the actual sheaf products and the canonical base-change projection. The map from Z₀ is the universal pullback lift; geometric Tor and chartwise flatness reuse the landed declarations cited in stmt_deps.
